provenance.not-tokens-only-and-real-behaviour: Confirming, not assuming, the same finding checkbox.m3.json and switch.m3.json both already recorded for this clone: radio/internal/radio.ts is real, full Lit component source, not a tokens fragment.
provenance.edition-pin: v0.192, per the owner's registry-wide decision. UNLIKE switch's own wholesale-redesign edition delta, radio's is a PLAIN FORMAT CHANGE ONLY: `latest`'s _md-comp-radio-button.scss replaces v0.192's `values()` function with a flat file of individually-annotated `$variable` declarations, but every VALUE is byte-identical between editions — diffed directly, confirmed line by line, no token gains or drops of any kind. Flagged as a genuinely SMALL delta specifically because switch's own note in this pipeline trained the expectation of a large one; this component does not have one.
provenance.no-native-input-first-divergence-from-ow: structure.native-input is OFF for this column — a first, in this pipeline, for M3: checkbox.m3.json and switch.m3.json BOTH confirmed a real native <input> in M3's own shadow DOM; radio.ts has NONE anywhere, grepped directly across the whole radio/ directory (`file` run on every .ts file first, per CLAUDE.md's grep-then-file rule). Role and checked state are set purely through `mixinElementInternals`'s ElementInternals object: `this[internals].role = 'radio'` (constructor) and `this[internals].ariaChecked = String(this.checked)` (updated()) — the FIRST component in this whole registry whose M3 column uses ElementInternals for role assignment rather than either a native element or an explicit HTML attribute.
provenance.primary/on-surface/on-surface-variant: md-sys-color.values-light()/values-dark(), v0.192 — the SAME hex pairs every M3 column in this pipeline resolves (#6750a4/#d0bcff primary, #1d1b20/#e6e0e9 on-surface, #49454f/#cac4d0 on-surface-variant). Re-derived here for a self-contained column, not borrowed.
provenance.icon-container-tokens: icon-size: 20px, hardcoded literal, both editions (the whole `:host` — width/height both equal this) — the SAME container-is-the-icon-size shape checkbox's 18px container/18px icon pair already showed, but even more literal here since there is no separate container box at all, only the icon's own bounding box.
provenance.no-border-no-background-on-container: CONFIRMED, re-checked specifically because every prior M3 column in this pipeline (checkbox, switch) DID draw a container-level border/background: `internal/_radio.scss`'s `.container` rule sets ONLY `display:flex; height:100%; place-content:center; place-items:center; width:100%` — no `border`, no `background`, no `border-radius` anywhere in the whole file. The visible ring a user sees is entirely the icon SVG's own `<circle class="outer">` with a masked-out centre (`<mask><rect fill=white/><circle fill=black/></mask>`), not a bordered/filled container the way Salt's and shadcn's own items are.
provenance.dual-circle-geometry: radio.ts render(): `<svg class="icon" viewBox="0 0 20 20"><mask id=...><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="white"/><circle cx="10" cy="10" r="8" fill="black"/></mask><circle class="outer circle" cx="10" cy="10" r="10" mask="url(#...)"/><circle class="inner circle" cx="10" cy="10" r="5"/></svg>` — geometry (cx/cy/r) is fixed SVG markup, not a themed CSS row; ONLY `fill` (both circles, inherited from the parent `.icon`'s own `fill` property), `opacity`, and `transform` (the inner circle only) are CSS-driven. `.outer.circle { transition: fill 50ms linear }`, `.inner.circle { opacity: 0; transition: opacity 50ms linear }` at rest.
provenance.checked-animation: `.checked .inner.circle { animation: inner-circle-grow 300ms easing-emphasized-decelerate; opacity: 1 }`, `@keyframes inner-circle-grow { from { transform: scale(0) } to { transform: scale(1) } }` — a real, CSS-driven grow-in, the geometry given a live row per CHECKBOX-MATRIX finding 11's lesson (a declared structure strategy must be given real CSS, not left invisible).
provenance.colour-tokens-are-interaction-invariant-: UNLIKE switch's track (whose hover/focus/pressed tokens literally EQUAL the rest token, a true no-op), radio's icon DOES recolour on hover/focus/pressed — but the THREE values are numerically IDENTICAL to each other (unselected-hover-icon-color = unselected-focus-icon-color = unselected-pressed-icon-color = on-surface; selected-hover/-focus/-pressed-icon-color all = primary) — re-verified directly against the token file specifically because switch's own finding trained the expectation of a true no-op, and this is a DIFFERENT shape: a real change from rest, but no differentiation AMONG the three interaction states themselves.
provenance.disabled-opacities-selection-invariant: disabled-selected-icon-opacity: 0.38; disabled-unselected-icon-opacity: 0.38 — IDENTICAL, and disabled-selected-icon-color: on-surface; disabled-unselected-icon-color: on-surface — ALSO IDENTICAL. Re-checked specifically because switch's own disabled-selected-handle-opacity: 1 asymmetry trained the expectation of one here too; there genuinely is none for radio — a real CONTRAST, not a repeat, confirmed by reading both entries side by side.
provenance.state-layer-and-cursor: state-layer-size: 40px (md-ripple, centred on the 20px icon). hover-state-layer-opacity 0.08 / focus-state-layer-opacity 0.12 / pressed-state-layer-opacity 0.12, the SAME edition-dependent trio every prior M3 column has flagged, unchanged for this component between editions. `:host { cursor: pointer }` PLUS an EXPLICIT `:host([disabled]) { cursor: default }` — the first M3 column in this pipeline to write a disabled-cursor override at all; checkbox's and switch's own M3 columns left `pointer` in place even when disabled.
provenance.no-group-no-radiogroup-role: CONFIRMED ABSENCE, grepped directly across radio.ts, internal/radio.ts, internal/single-selection-controller.ts, and _radio.scss: no `radiogroup` string anywhere, no fieldset, no wrapping custom element of any kind. Selection sharing is entirely a SingleSelectionController side effect, scoped to the connected root node via `querySelectorAll('[name="..."]')`.
provenance.arrow-key-controller: SingleSelectionController.handleKeyDown (internal/single-selection-controller.ts): listens for ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right, is RTL-aware (`getComputedStyle(this.host).direction === 'rtl'`), skips disabled siblings, unchecks+blurs every other sibling, checks+focuses the target, and dispatches a real `change` event — its own doc comment: 'Handles arrow key events... Using the arrow keys will select and check the next or previous sibling with the host's name attribute', and the class's own top-level doc comment states the design intent directly: 'provides root node-scoped single selection for elements, similar to native <input type="radio"> selection'.
provenance.radio-specific-validator: radio.ts: `override [createValidator]() { return new RadioValidator(() => this.selectionController.controls) }` — RadioValidator (labs/behaviors/validators/radio-validator.ts) loops EVERY sibling sharing the host's name to compute whether ANY is required and whether ANY is checked, a genuinely different, group-aware validator from CheckboxValidator (which checkbox's and switch's own M3 columns both reused verbatim for a single element's own state).
provenance.required-is-group-scoped: Radio class's own `required` property doc comment, quoted directly: 'Whether or not the radio is required. If any radio is required in a group, all radios are implicitly required.' — a real, sourced, group-wide effect from a per-item boolean, computed by RadioValidator's own loop.
provenance.no-warning-no-error-family: CONFIRMED ABSENCE, grepped directly: neither edition of _md-comp-radio-button.scss contains the string 'error' or 'warning' anywhere — radio has NO validation tone in M3 at all, the second sighting of this exact finding (switch.m3.json was the first).

state.rest.value: no container styling of any kind — the visible ring is the dot's own outer masked circle at on-surface-variant

state.checked.value: the outer ring's fill moves on-surface-variant -> primary AND the inner circle animates in (opacity 0->1, 300ms scale-grow)

state.hover.value: the icon's fill recolours (unselected: on-surface); the item container shows nothing, having no drawable surface of its own
state.hover.note: the most extreme version yet of the 'feedback lives on the glyph, not the container' finding switch's own track already showed

state.focus.value: the icon recolours to the SAME value as hover, plus a 12%-opacity state layer and a separate 44x44 md-focus-ring not reproduced here

state.pressed.value: the icon recolours to the SAME value as hover/focus (M3 does not differentiate icon colour among the three interaction states), plus a 12%-opacity ripple

state.disabled.value: 0.38 opacity on the icon only, IDENTICAL for both selected and unselected — a real contrast to switch's own asymmetric finding
